title: Basic opens form a basis of Spec A, and Spec A_f is homeomorphic to the open D(f)
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ its set of prime ideals with the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; for $a\in A$ let $D(a)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A: a\notin\mathfrak p\}$. Then (i) every $D(a)$ is open, and the sets $D(a)$, $a\in A$, form a basis of the topology: for every open $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ and every $\mathfrak p\in V$ there is $a\in A$ with $\mathfrak p\in D(a)\subseteq V$; (ii) for $f\in A$, with $A_f$ the localization of $A$ at $\{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $\iota:A\to A_f$, $a\mapsto a/1$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}A_f\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\mathfrak P\mapsto\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak P)$, is a homeomorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}A_f$ onto the open subset $D(f)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with its subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology, line 2987), parts (11) and (14): D(f) is the complement of the closed V(f), and for p not in a closed V(I) there is f with p in D(f) and D(f) disjoint from V(I) (so the D(f) form a basis); Lemma Tag 00E4 (lemma-standard-open, line 3207): Spec(R_f) -> D(f) is a homeomorphism; tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00E0,algebra-lemma-Zariski-topology; 00E4,algebra-lemma-standard-open).
